# Helping Your Midwife Find You

*A short guide from your Riverside community midwives*

## Hello from a midwife who gets lost

Hiya! I'm one of your Riverside midwives, and I'm the one in the team who always gets lost. Deb asked me to write this page because I have a lot of experience.

Where I come from, in the Philippines, we say the midwife is like family. When we come to your home, we want to come as a friend, not as a stranger with a clipboard. But a friend can only help if she can find your front door. At 3am, in the dark, with a baby on the way, we need to get to you fast.

So here is how you can help us. Don't worry, nobody is in trouble. This is a "make it easy" page, not a "you did it wrong" page.

## First things first: when we come to your house

Home birth cover starts from **37 weeks**. We tell everyone this at your booking visit, and then everyone forgets, so here it is again.

If your labour starts **before 37 weeks**, please don't wait for us. Go to the hospital, as we talked about together. We will be very happy to hear from you afterwards.

## How to call us

When labour starts, phone the **Riverside birth line**.

- **Riverside birth line: [add number here]**
- Please do **not** call my own mobile. The birth line goes to whoever is on call, and that person will be wide awake and ready for you. I might be asleep with my phone on silent, and then neither of us is happy.
- Save the number in your phone **today**. Write it on the fridge too. At 3am nobody remembers anything, not even their own name.

**When you call, tell us:**

1. Your name
2. Your address
3. Anything tricky about finding you (a house name instead of a number, a block of flats, a street that looks like ten other streets)
4. Anything we should know at the door (like a very friendly dog, see below)

**Then send us a pin.** The what3words app is actually very good, I was surprised. Or just share your location on WhatsApp to the birth line phone. Either way, we get a dot on a map, and the dot does not lie.

**If you are worried, or it feels like an emergency, call 999.** Don't wait for us.

## Finding your door (this is the big one)

I have been a midwife a long time, and I have had some adventures. Here are a few true stories. Names are changed to protect the innocent.

### Flat numbers can be tricky

I once drove around a block of flats in Everton for **20 minutes**. Flat 14 was not next to flat 13. Flat 14 was in a completely different building. In the end, I found it because dad was waving a tea towel out of the window. Best tea towel I have ever seen.

If you live in flats, please tell us:

- Which building or block
- Which entrance
- Which floor
- How to get in (buzzer? code? someone coming down?)

### Houses with names, but no numbers

Some houses have a name, not a number. Imagine a lovely cottage called something like "Rosemary Cottage" in a street of terraces. My sat nav was very sure that it was a chip shop. It was not. (I still bought chips, but that is another story.)

If your house has no number, please:

- Make sure the name is easy to see from the road, in the dark
- Tell us which side of the street you are on
- Send the pin! The pin helps most of all

### Wrong house

One night I walked into the wrong house. The door was open. A very nice old man was sitting there, and he was not at all worried. He gave me a Jammie Dodger anyway. I want you to know that I did not stay for a second biscuit. I found you in the end, I promise.

Please check that your house number or name is easy to read from the street. That helps us and it helps the nice old men of Liverpool.

### Balloons on the gate: the best idea ever

One family tied **balloons to the gate**, like it was a birthday party. It was the best idea I have ever seen. I found them straight away and I felt like a celebrity. Please copy them. Any colour is fine. Bright is better.

### Porch light on, please!!

In winter, dark streets all look the same. **Please put your porch light on at night** when labour starts. If you don't have a porch light, put on a hall light, or leave the front door light on. It's a small thing and it helps a lot.

### Someone at the door

If you can, ask someone to watch for us and wave us in. A partner, a friend, a neighbour, or a very brave auntie. If it is dark and cold, they can wait just inside the door with the light on. They can wave a tea towel if they want to.

## Parking

Two midwives come for the birth, and we usually come in **two separate cars**. So if you can, please find **two parking spaces** near your house. We know this is not always easy.

If you live in a **permit zone** (there are a lot around Anfield and Kensington), please:

- Ask the council for a **visitor permit** before the baby comes, or
- Have one ready to put on the dashboard

We have had parking tickets before, at 4am, while delivering a baby. It is not a nice thing to find on your windscreen afterwards.

## The last ten metres: getting inside

We carry a **lot**. Gas and air cylinders, the big bag, and sometimes the birthing pool bits. By the time we get to your door, our arms are tired. A clear path makes us very happy. Please can you:

- **Clear the stairs and the hallway.** No shoes, no washing baskets, no Lego. (Lego hurts. Everyone knows this.)
- **Move the pets into another room**, with the door shut. I love dogs, I really do. But there was once a lovely staffie, who loved me too much. He jumped on me every visit, and I nearly dropped the Entonox. I do not want to meet your dog while you are pushing, and your dog does not want to either. A shut door, a chew toy, and a family member for company is perfect.
- Leave the front door **unlocked, or have someone ready to open it**, so we don't have to knock and wait in the cold.

## Fridge checklist

Please cut this out or take a photo and stick it on your fridge. You can tick the boxes as you go.

**Before labour (do these in the last weeks):**

- ☐ I saved the Riverside birth line number in my phone
- ☐ I wrote the number on the fridge
- ☐ I know that home birth cover starts at 37 weeks
- ☐ My house number or name is easy to see from the street, in the dark
- ☐ I have a visitor permit (if I live in a permit zone)
- ☐ I have checked that there is parking for two cars
- ☐ I have balloons ready for the gate (optional, but very good)
- ☐ I know who will wait at the door

**When labour starts:**

- ☐ Call the Riverside birth line (not a personal mobile)
- ☐ Tell them my name, address, and anything tricky about finding me
- ☐ Send a pin (what3words or WhatsApp location)
- ☐ Turn on the porch light
- ☐ Put balloons on the gate
- ☐ Put the visitor permit on the dashboard or sort out parking
- ☐ Clear the hallway and stairs (no shoes, washing baskets, or Lego)
- ☐ Put the pets in another room
- ☐ Ask someone to wait at the door

**Emergency?** Call 999.

## One last thing

If you forget half of this, please don't worry. Phone the birth line, tell us where you are, and we will find you. We might be a little bit late, and we might be a little bit lost, but we will always come.

See you soon, as a friend. 💛

*Your Riverside Community Midwives*

---

Things to check before it goes out:

- **Birth line number:** I left a gap for it, since I didn't want to guess.
- **Calling guidance:** Your notes didn't say when to call (for example, how far apart the contractions should be). If the team has a standard line on that, it should go in the "How to call us" section.
- **999 line:** I added this for safety. Take it out if Deb would rather word it differently.
- **Pet and house names:** I didn't use the real dog name or the real house name, so no family can be recognised on the Facebook group. If you want Pippin to be a star, that's up to you.
